walkthroughs.body_html:
White light is a mixture of all visible colours.

A glass prism refracts each colour by a slightly different amount — red bends least, violet bends most — so the colours fan out into a spectrum. This is called dispersion. 🌈

The order, longest to shortest wavelength: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

The primary colours of light are red, green and blue. Mix all three and you get white light. This is how a TV screen works.

Watch out: this is different from mixing paint. Paint colours subtract from white light by absorbing colours.

A red object looks red because it reflects red light and absorbs the other colours.

Materials interact with light in three ways:

Transparent — light passes straight through (clear glass, clean water). Translucent — light gets through but is scattered (frosted glass, tracing paper). Opaque — no light passes through (wood, metal, you).

Opaque objects either reflect or absorb the light that hits them.

options: Violet
Green
Red
Blue

mcqs.q: A red T-shirt is lit by green light only. What does it look like?
options: Red
Green
White
Black

mcqs.q: How do you see a non-luminous object like a book?
options: Light from a source reflects off the book and enters your eyes.
Your eyes send out beams of vision that hit the book and let you see it.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
It is unchanged — only the speed differs.

mcqs.q: If one EM wave has a higher frequency than another, what is true about its wavelength?
options: It is also longer, because both increase together.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
It is shorter — wavelength and frequency are inversely related (c = f x lambda).

mcqs.q: Is ultraviolet light visible to humans?
options: Yes — UV is visible because it's right next to violet.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
No — even though it sits next to violet on the spectrum, its frequency is above the range our eyes detect.
Yes — UV is the colour purple.
